parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Palanivel and others (husband, wife, children, etc.)

facts_of_case: The respondent filed a private complaint stating that the marriage between the first petitioner and herself was solemnised on 03.12.2008 and they were blessed with a male child on 02.10.2010. The first petitioner filed a petition for divorce in HMOP.No.72 of 2010, which was allowed on 18.11.2014. The respondent then filed an appeal in CMA.No.5 of 2015, which was allowed on 27.01.2016.

legal_principles.principle: When a marriage has been dissolved by a decree of divorce and either there is no right of appeal against the decree or, if there is such a right of appeal, the time for appealing has expired without an appeal having been presented, or an appeal has been presented but has been dismissed, it shall be lawful for either party to marry again.
legal_principles.held: A plain reading of the aforesaid provision shows that it shall be lawful for either party to marry again after dissolution of a marriage only after expiry of the appeal time when no appeal has been presented; if any appeal has been presented only after dismissal of the said appeal.

legal_principles.principle: An appeal was filed in time, but without making any enquiry as to whether any appeal was filed against the order passed by the Sub-Judge, Dharapuram in HMOP.No.72 of 2010.

outcome.final_order: The petition to quash the proceedings against the accused is dismissed.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashing criminal proceedings
